topology.core_complement: solid torus with H1=Z generated by y

smooth_ambient_torsion_line.consequence: The ordinary Z2 flat line is locally trivial around the core meridian and does not by itself force an odd vortex.

square_root_defect.interpretation: The square root exists on the solid-torus complement but cannot extend through the core. It is a discrete Z4/quarter-holonomy defect with pi meridian flux.

existing_gauge_holonomy_match.match: The beta=1/4 charge doublet is exactly the conjugate pair -i,+i whose squares are the nontrivial Z2 holonomy.

forced_majorana_vortex.interpretation: A charge-two Majorana pairing channel around a pi-flux defect must wind once. The odd winding required by the previous defect audit is therefore discrete rather than fitted.

parameter_audit.new_structure: a singular square root of the ambient torsion line on RP3 minus gamma
parameter_audit.relation_to_existing_data: matches the already audited beta=1/4 gauge-holonomy doublet

theory_effect.remaining_gate: derive the square-root defect line and its core boundary condition from the S2T action, then prove the unique transverse mode carries the periodic longitudinal line

verdict: The smooth Z2 flat line alone cannot force an odd local vortex because the core meridian is twice the complement generator. However, its square root on the complement is canonical up to conjugation: chi(y)=+/-i. This quarter-holonomy branch has meridian holonomy -1, matches the existing beta=1/4 gauge doublet, and forces unit winding in a charge-two Majorana pair field. It supplies a non-fitted origin for the odd defect sector, while the extension of the resulting zero mode along the core remains to be proved.
